stories.headline: Merz-Trump rift over Iran remark triggers US troop withdrawal, tariff threats, and eventual phone-call patch-up
stories.summary: A cascade of events strained US-Germany relations this week: Merz had previously told schoolchildren that Iran was 'humiliating' the US, provoking Trump's public attack ('knows nothing') and threats of new 25% tariffs; the US then announced withdrawal of 5,000 troops from Germany and halted a 4,000-troop deployment to Poland. Merz doubled down at the Katholikentag by saying he 'would not advise his children to go to the US,' drawing further US criticism. A Merz-Trump phone call on Friday was described by Merz as 'good,' with both sides stressing agreement on Iran and Ukraine, though US adviser Grenell continued criticizing Merz publicly.

stories.headline: Germany's medium-range missile gap widens as US cancels Tomahawk stationing
stories.summary: The US formally scrapped its plan to station Tomahawk cruise missiles in Germany — a stopgap agreed in 2024 by Scholz and Biden — leaving a significant capability gap. Defense Minister Pistorius confirmed an official purchase request submitted 18 months ago remains unanswered and plans a Washington visit in late May to press the case; Germany is also exploring European and Ukraine-developed drone alternatives.

stories.headline: Pistorius makes surprise Kyiv visit, announces joint drone development with Ukraine up to 1,500 km range
stories.summary: Defense Minister Pistorius traveled unannounced to Kyiv and Zaporizhzhia, where Ukrainian forces demonstrated drone warfare capabilities he called far ahead of any Western army. Germany and Ukraine announced joint development of drones with ranges up to 1,500 km; Pistorius also called Putin's peace rhetoric a 'deception maneuver' and assessed Russia in a 'phase of weakness.' He participated digitally in an EU defense ministers' meeting in Brussels reaffirming Ukraine support.

stories.headline: AfD hits record 29% in polling, seven points ahead of CDU/CSU, as warnings of 'Weimar conditions' spread
stories.summary: A new INSA poll placed the AfD at a national record of 29%, seven points ahead of the CDU/CSU (22%), with both coalition parties losing ground. CSU leader Söder warned of 'Weimar conditions' and called the AfD 'the worst right-wing organization in all of Europe'; the Kremlin publicly celebrated the result. Concurrent state-level polling showed the AfD at 36% in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and above 41% in Sachsen-Anhalt ahead of September elections.

stories.headline: AfD's plans to take power in Sachsen-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern alarm democratic institutions
stories.summary: A leaked 94-page AfD 'government program' for Mecklenburg-Vorpommern revealed plans for a deportation police unit, rollback of cultural policies, and state-media reforms; the AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt announced it would replace 150–200 senior civil servants if it wins the September election. State interior ministers demanded emergency planning, constitutional lawyers assessed the plans, and CDU in Sachsen-Anhalt left open the possibility of a Linke-tolerated minority government to block an AfD premier.

stories.headline: Merz booed at DGB Trade Union Congress as welfare reform tensions with unions escalate
stories.summary: Chancellor Merz received boos and whistles from delegates at the DGB trade union federation's annual congress in Berlin after advocating for sweeping social reforms, including pension and labor market changes. Ver.di head Werneke subsequently accused Merz of bypassing unions entirely — unlike predecessors Merkel and Scholz — though a first meeting at the chancellery was announced for June. CDU secretary-general Linnemann criticized the heckling as a degradation of political discourse.

stories.headline: 104th Katholikentag in Würzburg draws Merz, Steinmeier, and political debate over democracy
stories.summary: Germany's major Catholic convention ran five days in Würzburg, drawing 74,000 attendees and prominent political figures including President Steinmeier (who opened the event and called for civic resilience), Chancellor Merz (who was met with climate-activist protests and hecklers), and Bundeswehr General Inspector Breuer (who warned Russia could be ready for war against the West by 2029). Steinmeier also publicly defended Pope Leo against Trump's criticism at the event. Both Merz and Steinmeier used the platform for broader political messaging.

stories.headline: Merz government faces historic approval collapse — coalition stability and Merz's leadership questioned
stories.summary: Multiple polls showed Chancellor Merz's approval rating at a historic low of 15%, with 81% rating his performance as poor; a YouGov survey showed only 16% satisfied with the coalition. Internal CDU tensions surfaced, with state premiers complaining Merz treats them like 'department heads,' and speculation about potential successor Hendrik Wüst intensified. A Bundesrat defeat on the relief premium further illustrated the government's difficulty maintaining governing majorities.
